title: Shooting probe focuses on single Amherstburg officer; Summoned by 911 call, police blocked from entering home where victim, kids were alone
article: Robert Scott Carpenter was killed by a single bullet and one Amherstburg police officer has been designated a "subject" officer by the province's special investigations unit.
Subject officers -- those whose actions could potentially lead to criminal charges -- are not required to talk to the SIU but "witness" officers have no choice.
Three Amherstburg police officers have been designated witness officers by the SIU and further designations may follow, said Jon Ansell of the SIU.
Carpenter, 37, was fatally shot at his 258 McCurdy Drive home by an Amherstburg police officer shortly after 7 a.m. Monday.
An autopsy conducted Tuesday at Hotel-Dieu Grace Hospital concluded Carpenter "died of trauma directly attributable to a single gunshot wound."
Investigators would not reveal where Carpenter was shot. His mother said Monday her only son was struck by a bullet in his femoral artery near his groin.

It isn't clear how many officers witnessed the shooting. At least two police officers were at the scene but it's possible some or all of the three witness officers arrived after the incident, said Ansell.
The names of the subject and witness officers have not been released. The SIU will not release names unless an officer or officer is charged with an offence.
Lawyer Andrew Bradie confirmed he has been retained by the Amherstburg police service but declined comment as the SIU investigation continues.
Three SIU investigators spent Tuesday questioning stunned neighbours in Carpenter's quiet, middle-class neighbourhood.
"It's a shocking thing because this is such a nice, quiet neighbourhood," said Stephen Taylor.
"Everybody's stunned a little bit because we never expected anything like this to happen."

Taylor said residents aren't scared or concerned and that life was starting to return to normal. Police tape still surrounds Carpenter's home but the secondary barriers erected about 200 metres away in either direction have been removed.
Carpenter had lived in his home for about three years with his common-law wife Lisa Stewart. The couple had two children -- three- year-old Sarah and two-year-old Noah.
Police arrived at the home after receiving a "disrupted" 911 call Monday morning.
A police source said officers arrived to find Stewart outside the home screaming. The children were inside.
A neighbour said she witnessed a struggle at the front door as an officer attempted to enter and someone inside tried to keep the door closed.
From outside the police tape, there appears to be a large hole in the wall just inside the front door.
A police source said Carpenter was shot by one officer after lunging at another with a knife. Two officers suffered non-life threatening injuries in the incident.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates incidents involving police and civilians involving serious injury, sexual assault or death.
